title: PesoPath: should a budgeting app send money to Mexico?
prompt: Our client is PesoPath, a US fintech startup with a popular budgeting app used mostly by Spanish-speaking customers. It is considering launching a money-transfer feature so users can send money to family in Mexico. Should PesoPath enter this market?

clarifying_answers.objective: Decide whether to launch, and whether it would be profitable within two years.
clarifying_answers.geography: US to Mexico transfers only, for now.
clarifying_answers.business_model: The budgeting app is free with a paid premium tier. Transfers would earn a fee on each transfer.
clarifying_answers.capabilities: PesoPath has no money-transfer licenses today; it would need a partner bank or its own licenses.

hidden_facts.hint: how big the remittance market is
hidden_facts.fact: Migrants in the US send about $60 billion a year to Mexico.

hidden_facts.hint: competitors, fees, or pricing in the market
hidden_facts.fact: Western Union and Remitly lead, followed by Wise and bank transfers. The average fee is about 3% of the amount sent, and it falls about 0.2 points a year.

hidden_facts.hint: PesoPath's users or how much they send
hidden_facts.fact: PesoPath has 2 million active users. A survey says 40% of them send money to Mexico, about $4,000 a year each.

hidden_facts.hint: costs, margins, or what it takes to build
hidden_facts.fact: PesoPath's cost to move money (partner bank, currency exchange, compliance) would be about 1.8% of the amount sent. Building the feature and getting licensed would cost about $15M upfront.

hidden_facts.hint: how much of users' transfers PesoPath could win
hidden_facts.fact: Pilot data suggests PesoPath could win 25% of its senders' transfer volume in year one.

math_answers.question: How much money could PesoPath move in year one?
What annual profit would that volume earn at today's average fee?
How many years until the upfront investment pays back?

ideal_structure: Market attractiveness: size, growth, fees, competition
Client fit: existing users, trust, Spanish-language brand
Economics: volume x (fee - cost), upfront investment, payback
How to enter: partner bank vs own licenses
recommendation: Yes, enter, but through a partner bank. Selling only to its own users, PesoPath could move about $800M in year one and earn about $9.6M at a 1.2-point margin, paying back the $15M in about 1.6 years. The big risk is fees falling 0.2 points a year, which would wipe out the margin in about 6 years, so PesoPath must also cut its transfer cost over time.
common_mistakes: Sizing the whole $60B market instead of PesoPath's reachable volume
Forgetting the licensing and compliance cost
